Question: Nebraska, the home of the AMC, changed its license plate scheme. Each old license plate consisted of a letter followed by four digits. Each new license plate consists of three letters followed by three digits. By how many times is the number of possible license plates increased?
Solution:
Use the standard interpretation that each letter position has \(26\) choices and each digit position has \(10\) choices, with repetition and leading zeros in the digit blocks allowed.

The old format has one letter position and four digit positions, giving
\[
26\cdot10^4
\]
plates. The new format has three letter positions and three digit positions, giving
\[
26^3\cdot10^3
\]
plates. Multiplication counts every plate exactly once because every assignment to the ordered positions produces one unique plate, and every allowed plate has such an assignment.

The multiplicative increase is the new count divided by the old count:
\[
\frac{26^3\cdot10^3}{26\cdot10^4}
=\frac{26^2}{10}.
\]
Thus the number becomes \(\boxed{\frac{26^2}{10}}\) times as large, choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
